test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18th November 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper bought 60 kg of rice at ₹42 per kg and mixed it with 120 kg rice at ₹52 per kg. At what rate (₹ per kg) should he sell the mixture to gain 20%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

CP of mixture = (60 x 42 + 120 x 52)/ 60 + 120

⇒ 8760/180 = Rs. 48.66 per kg

⇒ SP on 20% profit = 48.66 x 120/100 = 58.40 per kg

**∴ Required rate is 58.40 per kg.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

A shopkeeper bought 60 kg of rice at ₹42 per kg 

and120 kg rice at ₹52 per kg

**Formula used:**

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

**Calculation:**

Price of 60 kg rice = 60 x 42 = Rs. 2520

Price of 120 kg rice = 120 x 52 = Rs. 6240

Now mix the the both rice then

⇒ Price of mixture per kg = (2520 + 6240) / (60 + 120)

⇒ 8760/180 = Rs. 48.66 per kg

Selling price of per kg on 20% profit = 48.66 x (100 + 20)/100

⇒ 48.66 x 120/100

⇒ Rs. 58.40 per kg

∴ Required rate is 58.40 per kg.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Profit% = [(Selling price - Cost price) × 100] ÷ Cost price

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

Loss% = [(Cost price - Selling price) × 100] ÷ Cost price

Selling price at loss = Cost price x (100 - loss%)/100

Selling price at discount = Marked Price x (100 - discount%)/100

1c
